utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-70-I, the Prosecutor versus Nebojsa Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This afternoon, the Court is convened to conduct the initial appearance of Nebojsa Pavkovic. Mr. Pavkovic, could you stand, please. Can you confirm to me that you can hear the proceedings in your own language and are able to follow what has happened so far.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear everything and I have understood everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Now, may I take the appearances. For the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm Thomas Hannis on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm assisted by trial attorneys, Christina Moeller and Carolyn Edgerton on my right, and the case manager Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much and for the accused, Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can indicate for the accused, Chrissa Loukas as assigned duty counsel. I'd also indicate, Your Honour, that I was assigned this morning and I'm accompanied by Mr. Aleksic. Mr. Pavkovic has applied for Tribunal legal aid and has sought to have Mr. Aleksic as his assigned counsel. My understanding at this stage is that Mr. Aleksic is not on the list of eligible counsel and in the limited time available, the Registry has not been able to determine eligibility. However, Mr. Pavkovic has requested that Mr. Aleksic be present in court today for the initial appearance and I make an application in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Loukas, I was alerted this morning to the interest that Mr. Aleksic may have in the case and his current involvement in advising the accused, Mr. Pavkovic, and I'm grateful to him for the assistance he has been providing and would encourage him to continue to do that. Meanwhile I recognise his presence in the court. I'm happy to see him here and I'm grateful to you for proposing that he should be here.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the principal purpose of this hearing is to ascertain the position of the accused at this stage in relation to the charges against him. One thing that he might do is insist that the indictment, which is a very substantial document, is read in full. What is his position, Ms. Loukas, in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can indicate that the Defence waives the reading of the indictment and that has been discussed with Mr. Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Pavkovic, I have to ask you to stand just briefly once more, please. Can you confirm to me, first of all, for the purposes of the record of these proceedings, your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am Nebojsa Pavkovic, Colonel General of the army of Yugoslavia, retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was born in 1946 on the 10th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can you give me, please, the address at which you were residing immediately before you left to come to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my address is Belgrade, the street of Molerova [phoen], number 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavkovic, can I take it that you have seen the indictment in your own language and been able to read it in full?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have received the indictment. I have read it and I am fully familiarised with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And have you been able to take advice from a lawyer of your choice on the plea, if any, which you should tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have taken advice from a lawyer, and I have decided on my plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can I therefore proceed to take your plea from you now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Pavkovic, I am going to read certain parts from the indictment, the crucial elements, so that you will be able to tender your plea, and when I come to each of the five counts against you, I will ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty, and you should answer in respect of each of these charges separately as I come to them. Now, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I understand that fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pavkovic, the indictment charges you along with three others, two of whom have appeared before the Tribunal already in the same situation as you do now. That's Vladimir Lazarevic and Sreten Lukic, and one of whom has not appeared, that is Vlastimir Djordjevic. You're charged along with each of them that you are individually responsible for crimes alleged under Articles 3, 5 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. It is said that you planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation or execution of these crimes. However, by using the word "committed" in the indictment the Prosecutor does not suggest that you physically perpetrated any of the crimes charged personally. "Committing" refers to participation or being part of a joint criminal enterprise as a co-perpetrator. It is said in the indictment that the purpose of the joint criminal enterprise was, among other things, the expulsion of a substantial portion of the Kosovo Albanian population from the territory of the province of Kosovo in an effort to ensure continued Serbian control over the province. It is said that to fulfil that criminal purpose, each of you acting individually or along with the others, and indeed with other people both it is said known and unknown, that you significantly contributed to the joint criminal enterprise, using the legal and factual powers available to you. It is also stated that the joint criminal enterprise came into existence no later than October 1998 and continued until 20th June 1999, and it is said that the crimes which are alleged in the indictment were committed between the 1st of January and the 20th of June 1999. Now, that's the allegation of direct individual criminal responsibility. There is also an allegation that the crimes set out in Counts 1 to 5 were within the object of the joint criminal enterprise, or alternatively, that the crimes set out in counts 3 to 5 were natural and foreseeable consequences of the joint criminal enterprise. Now, separately from these allegations of individual criminal responsibility, there is an allegation which is made against you and the other three co-accused, that while holding positions of superior authority you were responsible for the acts or omissions of your subordinates. Now, that allegation is made in terms of Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. A superior is responsible under that Article for the criminal acts of his subordinates if he knew or had reason to know that they were about to commit these acts or had done so Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and failed to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent the acts or to punish the perpetrators. So these are the two separate bases on which it is said you are criminally liable. I turn now to the particular counts against you, numbers 1 to 5. The first of these is that by the acts and omissions set out in paragraphs 21 to 29 of the indictment, you along with your co-accused, other named persons in the indictment, and others known and unknown, planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of Count 1, deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(d) of the Statute of the Tribunal. To that charge, Mr. Pavkovic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to that charge in the indictment, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. I move then to Count 2, in which it is said that by the acts and omissions set out in paragraphs 21 to 30, and in particular paragraph 25, you and the others I've already mentioned planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of Count 2, other inhumane acts, in particular forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. To that charge, Mr. Pavkovic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 3 is in these terms: That by the acts and omissions set out in paragraphs 21 to 32 of the indictment, you and the others already mentioned planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of Count 3, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. To that count, Mr. Pavkovic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On exactly the same factual basis, you are charged with Count 4, also a charge of murder, but this time as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(A) of the Geneva Conventions. To that count, Mr. Pavkovic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And I now deal with the last of the five counts in these terms, that by the act and omissions set out in paragraphs 21 to 34 of the indictment, you and the others already mentioned planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted the planning, preparation or execution of Count 5, persecutions, on political, racial and religious grounds, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal. To that charge, Mr. Pavkovic, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I plead not guilty to that charge as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pavkovic. You may sit for the moment. In light of the pleas that you have tendered, these pleas of not guilty, the Registrar will be instructed to fix a date for trial when appropriate. Meanwhile, you will remain in custody, as I am certain you have already been advised. Now, Mr. Hannis, can you assist me with an indication of the likely date on which you will have complied with your initial obligation of disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm advised we can do that by the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Pavkovic, when you receive the documents you are bound to receive initially, that is the documents which have been submitted in support of the indictment and any statements that were taken from you, once you receive these, you have 30 days in which to submit to the Tribunal any preliminary motions which you wish to make. So that -- these are the only dates that you immediately need to be concerned about. You will be advised by your counsel of other significant dates as they approach.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have understood what you explained to me just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Loukas, is there any matter you wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, there isn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand Mr. Pavkovic has certain health problems. Is there anything that I need to be concerned about in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I covered that matter briefly with Mr. Pavkovic during my initial conference today and there is nothing that we need to alert Your Honour to at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it appropriate, do you consider, for me to direct the same question to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think it is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pavkovic, just finally, are there any matters that you wish to raise with me in connection either with the proceedings or the circumstances in which you've come here or the circumstances in which you are presently being detained?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as for the condition of my health, right now I am fit. And I have been fully made aware of the indictment, IT-03-70-I, and I have pleaded with the full awareness of it. As for my further treatment, specialist checkups are under way here at clinics in The Hague, and there is no problem in that respect whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Secondly, in relation to the question that you put, as for the way I have been treated ever since I arrived on Dutch soil, I have been treated fairly, ever since I was admitted by the official authorities of the Tribunal, as I was transferred to the Detention Unit, in terms of staying at the Detention Unit, also my contacts with the administration and the staff, the standard in that respect, and I have no objections whatsoever. On the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thirdly, I wish to thank you in particular for having made it possible for my Defence counsel, Mr. Aleksic, to attend these proceedings. I have authorised him to represent me pro bono in this case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should I retain control of this case, and at the moment I do not know whether it is a case which will remain with me a Pre-Trial Judge, but if I do retain control, what I would hope would happen is that any communications that have to be made on your behalf will be made through your counsel. You've started on a very firm footing of a good relationship with counsel present in court. It is of great assistance to the conduct of proceedings in this Tribunal when there is a good working relationship between the accused and his counsel. So I invite to you bear that carefully in mind as the proceedings progress. I'm extremely grateful to counsel on both sides for the assistance they have provided in expediting these proceedings this afternoon. And I now think it appropriate to adjourn the proceedings. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go I just wanted to clarify one matter on the record. I am assuming we will have some verification as to who the counsel is to whom that should be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. Thank you very much.
